# HC8 guide-only operator trial

An independent agent used only README, CUE schema, binary help and the public toy
generator. It created fresh private synthetic fixtures without implementation/test
source, real credentials, provider calls, global configuration or hook changes.

The initial one-layer example could validate a signature but did not demonstrate
shared/project sources or restrictive composition. The delivered example closes that
gap: two projects, six in-memory toy issuers, shared installation/organization/team/
personal sources and distinct in-project signed project sources. All 13 generated
JSON artifacts passed their CUE contracts. Regeneration refused an existing directory
without changing any of their hashes.

| Task | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Both projects, check and explain | Exit 0/authenticated, five layers and two controls each |
| Mandatory control | Full 1000000 PPM, hold, no maintenance, no tuner |
| Advisory control | Effective 600000..850000 PPM range, chosen 750000 by personal, 75ms, hold, no maintenance |
| Guide preference contradiction | Exit 1/preference_denied, expected/loaded/authenticated =5/5/5 |
| Guide revoked organization issuer | Exit 2/signature_invalid, counts 5/2/1, sourceOrdinal=1 |
| Global/subcommand help | Exit 0; check/explain discoverable without configuration |

The agent replayed these commands against the final binary identified in
[README](README.md). The original example-gap receipt and final raw outputs remain
retained privately. Guide-only success establishes the toy task, not protected real
enrollment, actual operator identity, installed state or attended production benefit.

The audit skill passed skill-creator's validator using an existing offline environment.
Manual routing selected signed-harness adoption and excluded ordinary Git/prose edits;
automatic activation in an installed coding agent was not tested. No app-kit source
or renderer changed; its existing stdlib CLI divergence remains explicit.
